comparison: Strong agreement on C-terminal binding site identification (C112-C113, C116, C118-C120, C171, C47-C48). Both evaluations affirm that HDX protection data combined with mutagenesis/truncation studies support the C-terminal region (454-470) as a critical G protein binding site. OpenEval notes 'converging HDX and functional data' while peer reviewers explicitly state the data 'support the conclusions' regarding this binding site hypothesis.

Strong agreement on Ric-8A protection patterns (C74-C76, C78, C82, C145-C146, C165-C166). Both evaluations support that Ric-8A protects the C-terminal helix and switch regions. OpenEval emphasizes 'differential deuteration patterns' and corroboration with EPR data, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'Ric-8A shares some key properties with GPCRs' in C-terminal helix interaction and note 'data are of high quality.'

Strong agreement on widespread structural perturbations (C45-C46, C56-C57, C59-C62, C64, C68-C69, C168-C169). Both evaluations support that HDX-MS demonstrates Ric-8A induces broad deprotection across the Ras-like domain. OpenEval describes 'widespread structural perturbations' while peer reviewers characterize it as 'broad increases in flexibility' and 'loosening of the tertiary structure,' calling findings 'novel and fascinating.'

Strong agreement on experimental methodology quality (C49-C55). OpenEval finds methodological details 'well-documented' supporting experimental validity, while peer reviewers state 'work is of high technical quality' and 'experimental design is rigorous.' Both affirm the quality of materials, methods, and peptide coverage documentation.

Agreement on GDP vs GTP comparison (C84-C86, C91, C170). OpenEval finds the HDX comparison between nucleotide states 'supported' and consistent with known structural transitions. Peer reviewers do not explicitly critique these findings and accept the reversibility argument central to the manuscript, stating 'data are of high quality and support the conclusions.'

Partial disagreement on mechanistic comparisons with GPCRs (C121, C137-C138, C144). OpenEval finds the comparison 'supported' though notes 'some aspects remain speculative.' Peer reviewers express 'UNCERTAIN' evaluation, requesting authors 'soften their tone' on C-terminus role and questioning whether there is 'a spectrum of relative unfolding' depending on GEF and α subunit identity, noting β2AR-Gs 'seems like a bit of an outlier.'

Agreement on uncertainty about Ric-8A structural model (C104-C106). OpenEval rates claims 'SUPPORTED' but notes 'models themselves lack experimental validation.' Peer reviewers express 'UNCERTAIN' evaluation, asking 'can this be validated by CD or other biophysical measures?' and noting 'one minor concern is the validity of the Ric-8A model,' identifying lack of atomic structure as 'a weakness of this work.'

Disagreement on HDX kinetics interpretation (C58). OpenEval finds observations 'SUPPORTED' as 'experimentally measured' though mechanistic interpretation is 'limited or speculative.' Peer reviewers express 'UNCERTAIN' evaluation, questioning whether HDX distinguishes protein-protein interaction effects from nucleotide-free state effects, asking if 'Ric8 truly stabilizes the open conformation' or simply the nucleotide-free form.

Agreement on physiological GEF role uncertainty (C15, C21). OpenEval finds background claims 'SUPPORTED' as appropriately cited literature. Peer reviewers explicitly agree with the assessment that Ric-8A's physiological GEF role is unclear, stating 'It is not really clear whether Ric8 is a physiological GEF' and suggesting it be referred to as 'having or displaying GEF activity but not necessarily be referred to as a GEF.'

OpenEval evaluates background on G protein structure and prior characterization work (C24-C39) as 'SUPPORTED' with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/context claims.
OpenEval evaluates HDX methodology principles (C41-C44) as 'SUPPORTED' as well-established background. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological background claims.

OpenEval evaluates GPCR mechanism literature background (C123-C136) as 'SUPPORTED' with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims providing context for mechanistic comparisons.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic interpretations (C141-C142, C147, C149-C158, C162-C164, C167) as 'UNCERTAIN,' noting some aspects are well-supported while others are speculative, particularly regarding Switch II conformations, efficiency limitations, and chaperone function connections. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these interpretive claims.
